findings.summary: Step 1's expected baseline ('clean working tree') is factually false — 8 files are already modified, including both files the plan touches — so the plan's own stop condition fires immediately and delivers no artifact.
findings.evidence_required: `git diff --stat` currently reports .ai/project.yaml, src/dev_orchestration/config/models.py, src/dev_orchestration/domain/run.py, src/dev_orchestration/workflow/runner.py, src/dev_orchestration/workflow/tiers.py, tests/config/test_models.py, tests/workflow/test_runner.py, tests/workflow/test_tiers.py (181 insertions, 5 deletions). Revise step 1 to record the actual pre-existing delta as the baseline and define the task's contribution as the delta-over-baseline, or obtain an explicit decision to commit/stash the in-flight ApprovalPolicy work first. The plan must state which, since 'stop and escalate' as written yields zero delivered work.

findings.summary: Steps 7 and 8 gate on absolute working-tree cleanliness ('sole unstaged delta is tests/config/test_models.py', 'no production or orchestration files changed'), which is unsatisfiable given seven unrelated files are already dirty — both gates fail regardless of execution quality, and the pre-existing ApprovalPolicy edit to config/models.py will be misread as a scope violation by this task.
findings.evidence_required: Restate both gates as baseline-relative: capture the baseline diff (e.g. `git diff > baseline.patch`) in step 1, then require that the final diff minus the baseline diff touches only tests/config/test_models.py. Explicitly instruct the reviewer and verifier that the ApprovalPolicy changes in src/dev_orchestration/config/models.py and tests/config/test_models.py:6,150-166 are pre-existing and not attributable to this task.

findings.summary: Step 4's mutation targets the wrong module binding: rebinding DENIED_COMMAND_TOKENS on the imported test module has no effect on denied_tokens(), which resolves the name from its own module globals at call time — the mutation would leave the test passing and produce vacuous 'mutation kills the test' evidence.
findings.evidence_required: Step 4 must name the exact target: rebind `dev_orchestration.config.models.DENIED_COMMAND_TOKENS` (see models.py:26, where the loop reads the models-module global), not `tests.config.test_models.DENIED_COMMAND_TOKENS`. It must also state that the frozenset is replaced wholesale (frozensets cannot be mutated in place) and record which specific assertion in the new test fails — the `denied_tokens(command) == {"push"}` equality, the `pytest.raises(ValidationError)`, or both.

findings.summary: The two strongest assertions in step 3 — that the ValidationError's wrapped cause is a DeniedCommandError instance, and that the cause 'attributes rejection to push' — are asserted without evidence that Pydantic v2 exposes them, and DeniedCommandError carries no structured token attribute.
findings.evidence_required: Run a probe against the installed Pydantic showing whether `ValidationError.errors()[0]["ctx"]["error"]` returns an object satisfying `isinstance(..., DeniedCommandError)`, and paste the output into the plan. DeniedCommandError (models.py:12-13) subclasses ValueError with no attributes, so 'attributes rejection to push' can only be message-substring matching on the f-string at models.py:44-48 — the plan must say so explicitly and acknowledge that assertion is coupled to the message wording. If the cause is not retrievable as a DeniedCommandError, step 10 converts this into stop-and-report and the task again delivers nothing, so this must be settled before execution, not during it.

findings.summary: Step 3 deletes an existing passing parametrized case, which the brief ('add a focused regression test') did not request and which makes the diff non-additive.
findings.evidence_required: Either confirmation from the requester that de-duplication is in scope, or a stated decision to keep tests/config/test_models.py:48 and accept benign overlap with the new dedicated test. Net coverage is preserved either way — the new test is strictly stronger than the parametrized case — so this is a scope-discipline question, not a coverage one.
